tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Heirloom site v2: "Proof instrument" (design and build brief)

The v1 site (the light "conservation record", live on GitHub Pages) reads like a document. v2 replaces its whole visual layer with a cinematic, image-rich, animated experience and deploys to Vercel. **Keep the data layer and tests:**
- `site/web/scripts/build-data.mjs` → `site.json` + `receipts/*.json` + types;
- `src/data/counts.test.ts`, `scripts/check-links.mjs`, `scripts/qa.mjs`, the OG render;
- the keyboard/roving logic in `Register.tsx`, the replay state in `Replay.tsx`, the deep-link and focus logic in `Receipt.tsx`.

Every number on the page comes from site.json. Copy is plain and honest: "candidate backports", no exploitability claim, and the exact Ubuntu claim sentence: "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it."

## Direction: "Proof instrument"
Heirloom is a master watchmaker for old software: it opens the case, examines every part, repairs what's broken, and **certifies** what it can prove. The visual world:
- macro photography of watch movements and engraved metal;
- a live **3D brass movement** (gears, a guilloché-engraved medallion);
- **guilloché** line-work (the security engraving on watch dials and banknotes, a sign of authenticity);
- brass on deep ink, hallmarks, serial numbers.

It should feel like a luxury product launch (Apple / Rolex / Linear quality) wrapped around real security evidence. No purple, no glow blobs, no generic bento grid.

**Palette (dark):**
- ink `#08090A` / `#0F1112` / `#16191B`;
- line `#23272A`, bone `#ECE6DA`, muted `#9A958A`;
- brass `#C8A86A`, highlight `#E6CB8E`, deep `#8A6F3E`.
- Verdict chips:

  | Verdict | Text | Fill |
  |---|---|---|
  | FIX READY | `#5BC98F` | `#0F2A1D` |
  | NOT AFFECTED | `#7FB2FF` | `#0F1D33` |
  | UNPROVEN | `#E8B44C` | `#2E220B` |
  | AFFECTED | `#FF6B5E` | `#33130F` |
  | NO PROBE | `#8D8A83` | `#1A1B1C` |

  Each keeps its symbol ✓ ○ ? ! –, and all pairs meet AA.

**Type:** Instrument Serif (giant display, italic accents) · Geist (UI and body) · Geist Mono (serials, CVE ids, hashes). All OFL and self-hosted.

## The experience, beat by beat (what the visitor sees)
1. **Opening (hero, 100vh).**
   - A **real-time 3D brass watch movement** fills the right two thirds: procedural gears meshing and turning, an engraved guilloché medallion with the "H" hallmark, PBR brass, studio lighting.
   - The scene parallaxes with the mouse; on scroll the gears turn faster and the camera dollies in.
   - The headline reveals word by word: "Old software, *kept honest.*" Then the sub line, then three live counters ticking up: **13** candidate backports · **0** false "not affected" · **1** question asked.
   - Magnetic CTA buttons: "Watch it work" / "Open the proof". A thin guilloché ring draws itself around the hallmark in the nav.
   - **Fallbacks:** a pre-rendered poster image of the same scene for mobile, reduced motion and no-WebGL.
2. **"It examines every part"** (photo section). A full-bleed **macro photograph of a watch movement** with slow parallax and a brass duotone grade. Over it, a large statement: "Django stopped patching 4.2 in April. Debian and Ubuntu still ship it." The real version strings slide in as engraved plates.
3. **"Watch it work"** (the scroll-driven campaign, a pinned section about 300vh).
   - A **3D-tilted register** (19×3 tiles) sits on a watch-bezel dial. As you scroll, the dial turns from Apr 7 to Oct 9, and advisories arrive in date order. Each tile **stamps in** with a brass flash.
   - Captions cross-fade from data:
     - "May 5 · 3 advisories · 3 candidate backports";
     - "Aug 4 · CVE-2026-15307 asks the owner one question" (a question mark pulses on that tile);
     - "Oct 1 · Ubuntu ships its 15307 patch";
     - "Oct 6 · Django amends it" (an **animated brass connector draws** from 87890 to 15307: "stacked on our own backport · PR #21 on #20");
     - "84429 reuses the answer without asking";
     - "Oct 9 · follow-up".
   - Counters update live. Mobile gets a vertical story, with tiles animating in as each step enters.
4. **The finding** (cinematic split).
   - Two engraved date plates, **Oct 1** and **Oct 6**, fly in from either side and lock together around a glowing "5 days" band.
   - Below them, a terminal card *types out* the real probe run on Ubuntu's tree: FAIL, FAIL, FAIL.
   - Then the verbatim claim sentence, plus "hand-written probe calibrated on Django's own fix commits". A raw-logs link.
5. **The register** (full detail).
   - The real table, styled as an engraved certificate (brass header, hairline rules, serials, sticky header, filter with counts).
   - Hovering a row shows a brass spotlight that follows the cursor. Clicking a cell opens:
6. **The receipt** (a certificate of proof). It slides in with a slight 3D tilt:
   - a guilloché frame band, an animated hallmark shimmer;
   - the **calibration triangle as a live instrument diagram**: three nodes, brass connectors drawing in, FAIL lights blinking red three times then PASS lights going green;
   - gates as an engraved checklist; PR/issue buttons; copyable checkpoint and trace ids.
   - Keeps the focus trap, Esc, focus return and the hash deep links.
7. **"The movement"** (method). A horizontal **gear train**: five interlocking 3D-looking gears (SVG, animated rotation) for Locate → Probe → Calibrate → Adapt & verify → Decide & publish. They turn as you scroll and each lights up with its one-line proof. The rule appears in giant serif: "Never trust a test that hasn't failed."
8. **The question.** The real GitHub exchange from issue #6, rendered as an elegant message thread:
   - Heirloom's question;
   - the owner's answer `adopt-upstream-tests`;
   - the precedent P001 sealed with an animated wax-to-hallmark stamp;
   - then #20 applied, #19 reused without asking, and #21 stacked (each card flips in).
9. **Proof in numbers.** Huge serif numerals with count-up: **0** false "not affected" vs **1** for the naive pipeline (a split versus card with a red/green reveal), 13 candidate backports, 19 advisories, **$0.22** model cost per CVE.
10. **Economics** (cfo.ai). Three scenario cards (Base/Bear/Bull) with a gentle 3D hover tilt and animated mini-charts drawn from the business-plan inputs. Hypotheses are labelled.
11. **Evidence locker.** A photographic backdrop (engraved metal or archive drawers, darkened) with a grid of PR cards (13) and issue cards (6) that fan in. Command snippets type out with copy buttons. Entire and neatlogs proof links.
12. **Finale.** Back to the 3D movement, zoomed out and slowing to a stop. "Every verdict is a test run you can open." The CTA, then a footer colophon with photo credits and "Built with neatlogs · Entire · cfo.ai during neatHack".

**Motion system:**
- Lenis smooth scroll; Motion (`useScroll` / `useTransform` / `useInView`) for every scroll effect;
- SplitText-style word reveals (custom, not GSAP);
- Emil timings for UI (≤300 ms, ease-out `(0.23,1,0.32,1)`);
- cinematic beats 600–1200 ms.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: everything becomes static, with poster images and no smooth scroll.

## Assets (real imagery, licensed)
- **Photography:** 4–6 Unsplash photos (Unsplash License; free commercial use; credited in the colophon): macro watch movement, engraved metal or guilloché dial, brass gears, archive drawers or library.
  - The session finds them with WebSearch/WebFetch on unsplash.com, downloads via `https://unsplash.com/photos/<id>/download?force=true`, then grades and compresses them with `sharp` to AVIF and WebP (each ≤180 kB, responsive `srcset`).
  - It records each id, photographer and URL in `site/web/ASSETS.md`.
- **3D:** `three` + `@react-three/fiber` + `@react-three/drei` (lazy-loaded chunk).
  - Gears are procedural (THREE.Shape with involute-ish teeth, extruded and beveled).
  - The medallion texture is a canvas-generated guilloché used as a normal/bump map.
  - Lighting is `RoomEnvironment` (procedural, nothing to download).
  - DPR clamped to 1.5; the frame loop pauses off-screen.
  - The poster is rendered once with Playwright into `hero-poster.webp`.
- **Procedural SVG:** guilloché rosettes and wave bands from `scripts/guilloche.mjs`, the hallmark seal, the gear-train SVGs.
- **OG card:** re-rendered in the new style (the 3D poster, the headline, the counters).


## Verification
- **QA** (`scripts/qa.mjs`, extended): screenshots at 390/768/1440/1920; the hero after the 3D loads; the campaign at its start, middle and end; the receipt open; reduced motion; a 10 s screen recording of scrolling (Playwright video) that the session reviews frame-by-frame. ## Direction: "Proof instrument"
Heirloom is a master watchmaker for old software: it opens the case, examines every part, repairs what's broken, and **certifies** what it can prove. The visual world:
- macro photography of watch movements and engraved metal;
- a live **3D brass movement** (gears, a guilloché-engraved medallion);
- **guilloché** line-work (the security engraving on watch dials and banknotes, a sign of authenticity);

**Palette (dark):**

**Type:** Instrument Serif (giant display, italic accents) · Geist (UI and body) · Geist Mono (serials, CVE ids, hashes). All OFL and self-hosted.

# Site progress (B7a / B7b)

Spec: `~/brief/FRONTEND-BRIEF.md`. Live URL: https://iamdflame.github.io/heirloom/

## Milestones
- [x] M1 Toolchain: Node 22.23 (NodeSource), Playwright Chromium (headless shell 156) + deps, `heirloom export --out site/data` refreshed (summary now 13 AFFECTED / 1 NA / 5 UNPROVEN, matching the README).

- [x] M4 Hero/abstract (numbers from site.json), Fig. 1 register (ledger sheet, sticky accession column with the double red margin rule, row totals, filter with live counts, roving tabindex with arrows/Home/End/Ctrl+Home/PageUp/Down), replay scrubber (range input, play over 8 stops at 1 s, aria-live status, ink-in with motion `m` + LazyMotion, default end state), the 87890→15307 connector (SVG in the right margin at ≥1280 px; inline text below that) and the `query #6` marker; mobile cards (<768 px); lazy Receipt sheet (right ≥768, bottom below) with Condition / Examination (calibration triangle, failing ids, gates, probe origin; Tabs per line) / Treatment / Evidence (copy buttons, reproduce command), `#HL-4.2-007` deep links, focus return to the cell
- [x] M5 QA cycle 1 (+ a verification run c2) — see below

## Decisions
- Toolchain resolved to Vite 8 / @vitejs/plugin-react 6 / TypeScript 7 / vitest 5 (current majors); Tailwind pinned to v3 and React to 18 per brief.
- Fonts (≤100 kB): the fontsource Newsreader latin opsz file is 132 kB alone, so `scripts/subset-fonts.sh` subsets it and instances wght to 400–500, keeping the full opsz axis (6–72): 81 kB. Plex Mono 400/500 are subset to ASCII plus the few marks used (7 kB each). Total ≈ 96 kB. Files live in `public/fonts/` so the display font can be preloaded at a stable URL.
- Seal: generated by `scripts/seal.mjs` (10-lobe blob with low-frequency wobble, ring + slab-serif H cut out with a mask, one flat colour `--seal`); `scripts/favicon.mjs` renders `favicon-32.png` with Playwright.
- Lucide has no GitHub icon any more; `GithubMark.tsx` inlines the mark.
- Theme: `data-theme` on <html> (light|dark) overrides `prefers-color-scheme`; stored in localStorage, applied by an inline head script before paint.
- Advisory titles/dates/URLs are not in the export (they come from Django's `security.txt`). `scripts/sidecar.py` (run locally with uv; uses `heirloom.sources.django_security`, no Python changes) writes `site/data/advisories.json` and `site/data/artifacts.json` (run dirs on the `artifacts` branch, pinned to its sha, for raw-log links). Both are committed; CI only reads them.
- Cells use the matrix verdicts (`site/data/matrix.json`), which agree with the campaign: AFFECTED on 4.2.30 with a PR = FIX READY (13); elsewhere AFFECTED. `no_calibrated_probe` = NO PROBE. Chip totals: FIX READY 13, AFFECTED 21, NOT AFFECTED 7, UNPROVEN 4, NO PROBE 12 (= 57 cells).
- Accession order: advisory date, then CVE year and number (numeric), so CVE-2026-5766 is HL–4.2–001.
- Replay stops come from data (EOL constant, advisory batches, CVE-2026-15830's follow-up on 10-09) plus the brief's 2026-10-01 "Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 patch". The noble changelog in `evals/distro_lines.json` is dated 2026-09-28; 10-01 is the brief's date, kept as the one editorial constant in `build-data.mjs`.
- Treatment run id: campaign_evidence's run (the run that did the work) beats the event's run id (a later resume that only published). Raw logs: that run's dir on `artifacts`, else the CVE's latest.
- Porter model names are not in the export, so receipts say "written by the independent porter" without a model (rule 8: hide what's missing).
- `site.json`/`receipts/` are build outputs (git-ignored); `npm run build` = build-data → tsc → vitest → vite build, so CI fails if counts drift from the README.
- Filter semantics: single-select; shows rows that have at least one cell with the chosen verdict and outlines the matching chips. Counts are live: they follow the replay position.
- Row total wording: "n of 3 lines affected", plus "· k undecided" when some cells are UNPROVEN/NO PROBE; "none of 3 decided" when no cell is decided (so a NO PROBE row never reads as "0 affected").
- Rows not yet arrived during the replay stay in place as empty ledger lines (accession only), so the sheet doesn't jump.
- Receipt: Examination uses Tabs (one per line); the clicked cell's line is preselected; a deep link opens on Django 4.2.30. Receipt JSON is fetched from `receipts/<CVE>.json` on open and cached.
- Data is bundled (`src/data/site.json`, ~6 kB gz) so the register renders without a fetch; `public/site.json` is the same file, published.

## QA cycle 1 (2026-10-12, `node scripts/qa.mjs c1`, 16 screenshots read)
Script results: axe 0 serious/critical on 10 runs (8 page views + receipt desktop/mobile); console 0 errors/warnings; keyboard flow PASS (Tab into register → ArrowRight/ArrowDown/End/Home → Enter opens #HL-4.2-002 → Esc closes → focus back on the same cell); deep link `#HL-4.2-018` opens CVE-2026-87890; replay middle reads "Aug 4 2026 · 15 of 19 advisories"; Lighthouse mobile 96 / 100 / 100 / 100; first-load JS 103.6 kB gz (budget 150), fonts 93.7 kB (budget 100). A pre-cycle run (c0) found axe `definition-list` (serious) in the receipt Evidence list (a copy button sat directly in the `<dl>` row), fixed before c1.

Defects seen in the PNGs:
1. **390 px: horizontal overflow.** The page renders 423 px wide: register cards grow to fit unbreakable mono identifiers in titles (`django.http.HttpRequest.get_signed_cookie`). (page-390x844-*)
2. **768 px: replay tick labels collide** ("Django 4.2 end of life" runs into "3 advisories"; "Ubuntu ships its…" into "4 advisories"). (page-768x1024-*)
3. **768 px: table clips** the Ubuntu column and the total column off the right edge (scrolls horizontally; sticky accession works, but half the row is hidden with no cue).
4. **1440/1920: "Lines affected" column too narrow**: "2 of 3 lines affected" wraps onto 3 lines, so rows are taller than the content needs; header "LINES AFFECTED" wraps too.
5. Lighthouse `label-content-name-mismatch`: filter toggles had an aria-label ("Fix ready, 13 cells") that differs from the visible text ("✓ FIX READY 13").
6. Receipt (390 px) Condition list: chips wrap under long line labels at different indents. Fixed between c0 and c1 (grid: label left, chip right); recheck in cycle 2.
7. Minor: the hero meta line breaks after "built" at 1440 ("built / during neatHack"), and the table leaves ~14rem of empty margin at 1440–1920 when the connector isn't the focus. Left as is: the margin holds the connector.

Fixes after cycle 1 (verified by re-running as `qa/c2` and reading the PNGs):
- (1) cards: `min-w-0` + `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on titles → the 390 px page is 390 px wide (page-390x844-light is 390×8673).

- (3) table: `table-fixed` + `<colgroup>` widths; the total column moves into the advisory cell below 1024 px → all three line columns fit at 768 with no horizontal scroll.
- (4) total column 11rem, each part nowrap ("2 of 3 lines affected" / "1 undecided") → one or two lines at 1440/1920. Long identifiers in titles get `<wbr>` after `.` and `_` instead of breaking mid-word.

- (6) receipt Condition rows on 390 px: label left, chip right, version below → checked in receipt-mobile.png.

## QA cycle 2 results (`qa/c2`)
axe 0 serious/critical (10 runs); console 0; keyboard PASS; Lighthouse mobile 96 / 100 / 100 / 100; first-load JS 103.7 kB gz; fonts 93.7 kB; lazy chunks: Receipt 4.9 kB gz + sheet (Radix dialog/tabs) 10.6 kB gz; site.json 24.7 kB.

- Lighthouse performance is 96, not 100: `render-blocking-insight` (~300 ms, the CSS file) and `max-potential-fid` 200 ms. Options: inline critical CSS, or split the 404 entry so `src-*.js` (react-dom) isn't shared as a separate preload.

- Advisory titles/dates/URLs are not in the export (they come from Django's `security.txt`). `scripts/sidecar.py` (run locally with uv; uses `heirloom.sources.django_security`, no Python changes) writes `site/data/advisories.json` and `site/data/artifacts.json` (run dirs on the `artifacts` branch, pinned to its sha, for raw-log links). Both are committed; CI only reads them.
- Cells use the matrix verdicts (`site/data/matrix.json`), which agree with the campaign: AFFECTED on 4.2.30 with a PR = FIX READY (13); elsewhere AFFECTED. `no_calibrated_probe` = NO PROBE. Chip totals: FIX READY 13, AFFECTED 21, NOT AFFECTED 7, UNPROVEN 4, NO PROBE 12 (= 57 cells).
- Accession order: advisory date, then CVE year and number (numeric), so CVE-2026-5766 is HL–4.2–001.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rebuilds the self-hosted font files in public/fonts (latin only, total <= 100 kB).
# Newsreader: the fontsource latin opsz file, subset, then instanced to wght 400-500 (opsz 6-72 kept).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
NR=node_modules/@fontsource-variable/newsreader/files/newsreader-latin-opsz-normal.woff2
PM=node_modules/@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono/files
OUT=public/fonts
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
FT="uvx --from fonttools --with brotli"
$FT pyftsubset "$NR" --unicodes="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF,U+2013,U+2014,U+2018,U+2019,U+201C,U+201D,U+2022,U+2026,U+00B7,U+2070-209F,U+2191,U+2192,U+2212,U+00D7,U+2713,U+25CB" \
  --layout-features='kern,liga,lnum,tnum,onum,pnum,case' --flavor=woff2 --output-file="$TMP/nr.woff2"
$FT fonttools varLib.instancer "$TMP/nr.woff2" wght=400:500 -o "$TMP/nr-i.woff2"
$FT python -c "from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont; f=TTFont('$TMP/nr-i.woff2'); f.flavor='woff2'; f.save('$OUT/newsreader-latin-opsz-wght400-500.woff2')"
for w in 400 500; do
  $FT pyftsubset "$PM/ibm-plex-mono-latin-$w-normal.woff2" \
    --unicodes="U+0020-007E,U+00A0,U+00B7,U+00D7,U+2013,U+2014,U+2019,U+2026,U+207A,U+207B,U+2192,U+2212,U+2713,U+25CB" \
    --layout-features='kern,tnum,case,zero' --flavor=woff2 --output-file="$OUT/ibm-plex-mono-latin-$w.woff2"
done
ls -la "$OUT"

cat > scripts/subset-fonts.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rebuilds the self-hosted font files in public/fonts (latin subset, OFL).
# Instrument Serif 400 normal + italic (display), Geist variable 400-600 (UI/body), Geist Mono variable 400-500.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
IS=node_modules/@fontsource/instrument-serif/files
GS=node_modules/@fontsource-variable/geist/files/geist-latin-wght-normal.woff2
GM=node_modules/@fontsource-variable/geist-mono/files/geist-mono-latin-wght-normal.woff2
OUT=public/fonts
rm -f "$OUT"/*.woff2 "$OUT"/LICENSE-*.txt
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
FT="uvx --from fonttools --with brotli"
U="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF,U+2013,U+2014,U+2018,U+2019,U+201C,U+201D,U+2022,U+2026,U+00B7,U+2070-209F,U+2191,U+2192,U+2212,U+00D7,U+2713,U+25CB,U+2190,U+2193,U+2197"
for s in normal italic; do
  $FT pyftsubset "$IS/instrument-serif-latin-400-$s.woff2" --unicodes="$U" \
    --layout-features='kern,liga,lnum,tnum,case' --flavor=woff2 --output-file="$OUT/instrument-serif-400-$s.woff2"
done
$FT fonttools varLib.instancer "$GS" wght=400:600 -o "$TMP/g.woff2"
$FT pyftsubset "$TMP/g.woff2" --unicodes="$U" --layout-features='kern,liga,tnum,case,ss01' --flavor=woff2 --output-file="$OUT/geist-wght400-600.woff2"
$FT fonttools varLib.instancer "$GM" wght=400:500 -o "$TMP/gm.woff2"
$FT pyftsubset "$TMP/gm.woff2" --unicodes="$U" --layout-features='kern,tnum,case,zero' --flavor=woff2 --output-file="$OUT/geist-mono-wght400-500.woff2"
cp node_modules/@fontsource/instrument-serif/LICENSE "$OUT/LICENSE-instrument-serif.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
cp node_modules/@fontsource-variable/geist/LICENSE "$OUT/LICENSE-geist.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
ls -la "$OUT"
EOF
bash scripts/subset-fonts.sh 2>&1 | tail -8

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

import sharp from 'sharp';
import { mkdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const SRC = process.argv[2];
if (!SRC) throw new Error('usage: node scripts/photos.mjs <raw dir>');
const OUT = new URL('../public/photos/', import.meta.url).pathname;
mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });
export const PHOTOS = [
  { name: 'movement', id: 'HmIwomthlWw' },
  { name: 'gears-dark', id: 'snk-X32c8tE' },
  { name: 'dial', id: 'FCsA8Adcgr4' },
  { name: 'gears-brass', id: 'UQ2Fw_9oApU' },
  { name: 'archive', id: 'Ph4ZJrwf4x8' },
  { name: 'watch-dark', id: 'LaFLlEKx1c0' },
];
const WIDTHS = [640, 1280, 1920];
const MAX = 180 * 1024;
// 70% brass duotone (luminance × [1, .82, .55]) + 30% of the original colour
const L = [0.3, 0.59, 0.11];
const mix = (k, i) => L.map((l, j) => +(0.7 * k * l + (i === j ? 0.3 : 0)).toFixed(4));
const RECOMB = [mix(1, 0), mix(0.82, 1), mix(0.55, 2)];
const vignette = (w, h) =>
  Buffer.from(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${w}" height="${h}"><defs><radialGradient id="v" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="75%">
  <stop offset="40%" stop-color="#fff"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3a3a3a"/></radialGradient></defs><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="url(#v)"/></svg>`);

const manifest = {};
for (const p of PHOTOS) {
  const base = sharp(join(SRC, `${p.id}.jpg`)).rotate();
  const meta = await base.metadata();
  manifest[p.name] = { id: p.id, ratio: +(meta.width / meta.height).toFixed(4), widths: [] };
  for (const w of WIDTHS) {
    if (w > meta.width) continue;
    const h = Math.round((w * meta.height) / meta.width);
    const graded = await sharp(join(SRC, `${p.id}.jpg`))
      .rotate()
      .resize(w)
      .recomb(RECOMB)
      .linear(0.82, -6)
      .gamma(1.15)
      .composite([{ input: vignette(w, h), blend: 'multiply' }])
      .toBuffer();
    for (const [fmt, opts] of [['avif', { quality: 50, effort: 6 }], ['webp', { quality: 70, effort: 6 }]]) {
      let q = opts.quality;
      let file;
      for (;;) {
        file = join(OUT, `${p.name}-${w}.${fmt}`);
        await sharp(graded)[fmt]({ ...opts, quality: q }).toFile(file);
        if (statSync(file).size <= MAX || q <= 25) break;
        q -= 8;
      }
      console.log(`${p.name}-${w}.${fmt} ${(statSync(file).size / 1024).toFixed(0)} kB q${q}`);
    }
    manifest[p.name].widths.push(w);
  }
}
writeFileSync(new URL('../src/data/photos.json', import.meta.url), JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 1) + '\n');
EOF

// to public/photos/<name>-<w>.{avif,webp}, each <= 180 kB. Usage: node scripts/photos.mjs <dir of <id>.jpg>
import sharp from 'sharp';
import { mkdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const SRC = process.argv[2];
if (!SRC) throw new Error('usage: node scripts/photos.mjs <raw dir>');
const OUT = new URL('../public/photos/', import.meta.url).pathname;
mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });
export const PHOTOS = [
  { name: 'movement', id: 'HmIwomthlWw' },
  { name: 'gears-dark', id: 'snk-X32c8tE' },
  { name: 'dial', id: 'FCsA8Adcgr4' },
  { name: 'gears-brass', id: 'UQ2Fw_9oApU' },
  { name: 'archive', id: 'Ph4ZJrwf4x8' },
  { name: 'watch-dark', id: 'LaFLlEKx1c0' },
];
const WIDTHS = [640, 1280, 1920];
const MAX = 180 * 1024;
// 70% brass duotone (luminance × [1, .82, .55]) + 30% of the original colour
const L = [0.3, 0.59, 0.11];
const mix = (k, i) => L.map((l, j) => +(0.7 * k * l + (i === j ? 0.3 : 0)).toFixed(4));
const RECOMB = [mix(1, 0), mix(0.82, 1), mix(0.55, 2)];
const vignette = (w, h) =>
  Buffer.from(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${w}" height="${h}"><defs><radialGradient id="v" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="75%">
  <stop offset="40%" stop-color="#fff"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3a3a3a"/></radialGradient></defs><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="url(#v)"/></svg>`);

const manifest = {};
for (const p of PHOTOS) {
  const base = sharp(join(SRC, `${p.id}.jpg`)).rotate();
  const meta = await base.metadata();
  manifest[p.name] = { id: p.id, ratio: +(meta.width / meta.height).toFixed(4), widths: [] };
  for (const w of WIDTHS) {
    if (w > meta.width) continue;
    const h = Math.round((w * meta.height) / meta.width);
    const graded = await sharp(join(SRC, `${p.id}.jpg`))
      .rotate()
      .resize(w)
      .recomb(RECOMB)
      .linear(0.82, -6)
      .gamma(1.15)
      .composite([{ input: vignette(w, h), blend: 'multiply' }])
      .toBuffer();
    for (const [fmt, opts] of [['avif', { quality: 50, effort: 6 }], ['webp', { quality: 70, effort: 6 }]]) {
      let q = opts.quality;
      let file;
      for (;;) {
        file = join(OUT, `${p.name}-${w}.${fmt}`);
        await sharp(graded)[fmt]({ ...opts, quality: q }).toFile(file);
        if (statSync(file).size <= MAX || q <= 25) break;
        q -= 8;
      }
      console.log(`${p.name}-${w}.${fmt} ${(statSync(file).size / 1024).toFixed(0)} kB q${q}`);
    }
    manifest[p.name].widths.push(w);
  }
}

content.content:
name: pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'evals/*.json'
      - 'docs/business-plan.md'
      - 'README.md'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: site/web
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: site/web/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: site/web/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
README: live site link; hackathon.md: site entry with QA numbers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
